name: net_reconnect_live
description: Against the real server (a dev match, classic:2): once a checkpoint past tick 0 is kept, the second game's link drops (its socket closes at once, without a close frame: a drop, not a goodbye) and the game is busy for 6 s, so the server hears nothing and its seat goes AWAY: the caretaker plays it, and the other game sees it so. Then the game opens a new link with a resume HELLO (the same token, the match and the wire seat it held): MATCH_CONFIG(rejoin), RESYNC(rejoin) from the latest agreed checkpoint, its parts and the turns since, paced by the server's catch-up. It loads the checkpoint, catches up, says shown, is BACK, and gets its seat back at the next build window; both play on, and their hash streams are equal at every tick both printed.

steps.msg: the partner's silence put its seat AWAY; my world is live
the partner's seat came back, and the match runs on
no desync, and nothing resynced me

steps.assert: not Game.accepts_commands() and scene.client.held_match >= 1 and scene.client.held_seat == scene.client.seat - 1 and scene.overlay().state == 1
steps.msg: reconnecting, orders waiting, holding its match and seat; the overlay says so

steps.assert: scene.client.resumes >= 1 and scene.client.token == token and scene.client.resyncs[0][0] == 'rejoin' and scene.client.resyncs[0][1] > 0
steps.msg: a resume HELLO with the same token took the seat back: RESYNC(rejoin) from a checkpoint past tick 0
its seat was handed back at a build window, and orders go out again
